AfterRoomEntered.rationale: BronzeScales.cs:11-18 applies PowerVar<ThornsPower>(3m).BaseValue to its owner on AfterRoomEntered when the room `is CombatRoom`. The sim uses on_combat_start, the combat-scoped hook, with the same amount and the same applier (the owner). Same observable: the game's room-entered hook for a combat room fires as the combat room is set up, and Thorns is a per-combat power on both sides, so the player enters every fight -- and only a fight -- with 3 Thorns. The sim's Relic base does expose a run-level after_room_entered (relics/base.py:194), and using it would have been the literal mapping; the combat hook is the better one here because the sim's rooms and combats are separate objects and the power belongs to the combat. Contrast relic/big_mushroom, whose AfterRoomEntered is genuinely run-level (a sprite scale) and is waived as presentation.

guards.what: N1: the `room is CombatRoom` type test (BronzeScales.cs:13)
guards.rationale: This is the whole reason the divergent hook choice is safe: C# fires AfterRoomEntered for EVERY room and self-filters to combat rooms, so binding the port to on_combat_start reproduces the filter for free. A port that used the sim's run-level after_room_entered without a room-type check would grant Thorns outside combat, where the sim has no power container to hold it.

guards.what: N2: DynamicVars["ThornsPower"].BaseValue (BronzeScales.cs:16) -- the key is the POWER TYPE NAME, not 'Thorns'
guards.rationale: PowerVar<ThornsPower>(3m) (line 7) registers under the generic argument's type name, which is why the read at line 16 is the keyed form rather than a `DynamicVars.Thorns` property. Value 3, no AscensionHelper branch in the file, and the sim's literal 3 matches. Recorded because the same relic family uses both spellings -- relic/akabeko reads DynamicVars["VigorPower"] while relic/bag_of_marbles reads DynamicVars.Vulnerable -- and picking the wrong var silently yields 0.

guards.what: N3: Flash() and the Thorns hover tip (BronzeScales.cs:9, 15)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
